title: Bike Data Lakehouse: Medallion End-to-End with Star Schema
evaluates: Ability to design and implement a full medallion (bronze/silver/gold) lakehouse on Databricks: catalog/schema/volume provisioning, raw CSV ingestion to Delta, data cleaning and standardization in PySpark, dimensional modeling (star schema) in Spark SQL, surrogate keys, and notebook-based orchestration as job entry points.
requirements: Create a Unity Catalog catalog (workspace), bronze/silver/gold schemas, and a raw_sources volume (init_lakehouse.ipynb).
Ingest 6 source CSVs from CRM and ERP systems into bronze Delta tables driven by a config list (bronze improved) or one cell per file (bronze basic).
Build 6 silver Delta tables with trimming, normalization, deduplication, type casting, derived columns, and column renaming.

Build the gold star schema: dim_customers (CRM+ERP join with gender coalescing and ROW_NUMBER surrogate key), dim_products (CRM+ERP category enrichment with surrogate key), and fact_sales (sales joined to both dimensions on surrogate keys).
Wire silver_orchestration and gold_orchestration notebooks with dbutils.notebook.run to act as single job entry points per layer.

preview: Complete real-world medallion lakehouse on Databricks: provision catalog/schemas/volume, ingest CRM+ERP CSVs into bronze, clean and standardize into silver, then model a gold star schema (dim_customers, dim_products, fact_sales) with surrogate keys and per-layer orchestration notebooks.
portfolio_value: Flagship portfolio piece: demonstrates the entire modern data engineering loop on a pure-Databricks stack (Unity Catalog, Delta, PySpark, Spark SQL) with real medallion architecture and dimensional modeling. Recruiters recognize the DataWithBaraa Bike Lakehouse as a substantive, end-to-end build.
notes: Two bronze variants are provided (basic = one cell per file, improved = config-driven loop). Gold layer must run after silver because fact_sales joins to gold dim tables on surrogate keys. Targets workspace catalog; adjust catalog name if not using the default Unity Catalog workspace.

title: Provision Lakehouse: Catalog, Schemas and Volume
evaluates: Provisioning Unity Catalog objects with Spark SQL: selecting a catalog, creating bronze/silver/gold schemas with comments, and creating a managed volume for raw file landing.
requirements: USE CATALOG workspace.
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS for bronze, silver, gold with descriptive comments.
CREATE VOLUME IF NOT EXISTS workspace.bronze.raw_sources for raw CSV files.
preview: Set up the Unity Catalog foundation: pick the workspace catalog, create the three medallion schemas with comments, and create a volume to land raw CSV source files.
portfolio_value: Shows familiarity with Unity Catalog governance primitives (catalog/schema/volume) that gate every Databricks lakehouse project.
notes: Idempotent DDL (IF NOT EXISTS). Must run first; everything downstream writes into these schemas.

title: Bronze Ingestion: CRM + ERP CSVs to Delta (config-driven)
evaluates: Config-driven raw ingestion: iterating over an INGESTION_CONFIG list of source/path/table dicts, reading CSV from a volume with header+inferSchema, and writing each as an overwrite Delta table into the bronze schema.
requirements: Define an INGESTION_CONFIG list covering 3 CRM and 3 ERP source files.
Loop over the config, read each CSV (header=true, inferSchema=true) from /Volumes/workspace/bronze/raw_sources/...
Write each DataFrame as overwrite Delta saveAsTable into workspace.bronze.<table>.
preview: Ingest six raw CRM/ERP CSVs into bronze Delta tables using a single config-driven loop instead of repeated copy-paste cells.
portfolio_value: Demonstrates the DRY/config-driven ingestion pattern data engineers use to scale ingestion without duplicating code per source.
notes: A simpler 'basic' variant (one cell per file) exists at script/bronze/bronze_layer(basic).ipynb for comparison. Requires source CSVs already uploaded into the raw_sources volume.

title: Bronze Ingestion: One Cell Per Source (basic)
evaluates: Basic explicit raw ingestion: reading each CSV and writing it to its own bronze Delta table, one cell per source file.
requirements: Read each of the 6 source CSVs with header+inferSchema.
Write each as overwrite saveAsTable into the matching workspace.bronze.<table>.
preview: Beginner-friendly bronze ingestion that writes one Delta table per source CSV with an explicit cell each, before refactoring into the config-driven loop.
portfolio_value: Good first-step exercise showing the spark.read.csv -> saveAsTable round trip; pairs with the improved version to show refactoring instinct.
notes: Functionally equivalent to the improved variant but verbose; intended as the teaching baseline.

title: Silver CRM: Clean & Standardize Customer Info
evaluates: Silver cleaning of CRM customers: trimming all string columns, normalizing marital_status and gender coded values to readable labels, dropping rows with null customer_id, and renaming columns to a business-friendly schema.
requirements: Trim every StringType column generically.
Map cst_marital_status S/M to Single/Married and cst_gndr F/M to Female/Male with n/a fallback.
Filter out records with null cst_id.
Apply a RENAME_MAP to business-friendly names and write workspace.silver.crm_customers.
preview: Transform raw CRM customer rows into a clean silver table: trim strings, decode marital-status/gender codes, drop null IDs, and rename to a tidy schema.
portfolio_value: Canonical silver-layer cleaning task showing generic trimming, value normalization, null filtering, and schema standardization in PySpark.
notes: Reads workspace.bronze.crm_cust_info. Feeds gold dim_customers as the primary customer source.

title: Silver CRM: Parse Product Keys & Normalize Product Info
evaluates: Silver cleaning of CRM products: deriving category_id and a clean product_number from a composite prd_key via substring/regexp_replace, coalescing null costs to zero, normalizing the product line code, casting start date, and renaming columns.
requirements: Trim all string columns.
Split prd_key into cat_id (first 5 chars, dash->underscore) and a trimmed product_number.
Coalesce prd_cost null to 0; map product line M/R/S/T to Mountain/Road/Other Sales/Touring.
Cast prd_start_dt to DateType, apply RENAME_MAP, write workspace.silver.crm_products.
preview: Clean raw CRM products: parse a composite key into category_id + product_number, handle null cost, decode the product-line code, cast the date, and rename.
portfolio_value: Shows real string-parsing/feature-derivation (substring + regexp_replace) and defensive null handling that interviewers probe for.
notes: Reads workspace.bronze.crm_prd_info. The derived category_id is the join key to erp_product_category in gold dim_products.

title: Silver CRM: Clean Sales Dates, Prices & Amounts
evaluates: Silver cleaning of CRM sales: validating and parsing yyyyMMdd integer dates (order/ship/due) with length and zero checks, recomputing invalid/null prices from sales/quantity, and renaming to the silver schema.
requirements: Trim all string columns.
Convert integer dates to DateType only when length==8 and value!=0, else null.
Recompute sls_price = sls_sales/sls_quantity when price is null or <= 0 (and quantity != 0).
Apply RENAME_MAP and write workspace.silver.crm_sales.
preview: Repair messy sales data: parse integer yyyyMMdd dates safely, reconstruct invalid prices from sales/quantity, and rename to a clean fact source.
portfolio_value: Strong data-quality exercise: defensive date parsing and business-rule price reconstruction are exactly the edge-case logic that separates juniors from mid-levels.
notes: Reads workspace.bronze.crm_sales_details. This is the grain source for gold fact_sales.

title: Silver ERP: Clean Customer Demographics (AZ12)
evaluates: Silver cleaning of ERP customer demographics: stripping a 'NAS' prefix from customer ids, nulling future birthdates, normalizing gender variants, and renaming columns.
requirements: Trim all string columns.
If cid starts with 'NAS', strip the first 3 chars.
Set bdate to null when it is in the future; normalize gen (F/FEMALE, M/MALE) to Female/Male/n-a.
Apply RENAME_MAP and write workspace.silver.erp_customers.
preview: Standardize ERP customer demographics: fix prefixed IDs, null impossible birthdates, normalize gender, and rename for joining to CRM customers.
portfolio_value: Demonstrates cross-system key reconciliation (matching ERP customer_number to CRM) and demographic data hygiene.
notes: Reads workspace.bronze.erp_cust_az12. Supplies birth_date and fallback gender to gold dim_customers.

title: Silver ERP: Normalize Customer Location (A101)
evaluates: Silver cleaning of ERP location: removing dashes from customer ids and normalizing country codes (DE, US/USA, blank/null) to full names, then renaming.
requirements: Trim all string columns.
Strip dashes from cid via regexp_replace.
Map DE->Germany, US/USA->United States, blank/null->n/a, else passthrough.
Apply RENAME_MAP and write workspace.silver.erp_customer_location.
preview: Clean ERP location data: normalize customer keys and decode country codes into full country names for the customer dimension.
portfolio_value: Simple but realistic reference-data normalization task feeding the country attribute of dim_customers.
notes: Reads workspace.bronze.erp_loc_a101. Joins to CRM customers by customer_number in gold.

title: Silver ERP: Product Category & Maintenance Flag (G1V2)
evaluates: Silver cleaning of ERP product categories: trimming strings, converting a YES/NO maintenance text flag to a real boolean, and renaming columns.
requirements: Trim all string columns.
Convert maintenance YES/NO to boolean True/False (else null).
Apply RENAME_MAP and write workspace.silver.erp_product_category.
preview: Normalize ERP product categories and turn the YES/NO maintenance text into a proper boolean flag for the product dimension.
portfolio_value: Shows correct type coercion (text flag to boolean) and category reference cleaning for dimensional enrichment.
notes: Reads workspace.bronze.erp_px_cat_g1v2. Provides category/subcategory/maintenance_flag to gold dim_products via category_id.

title: Silver Orchestration: Single Entry Point
evaluates: Building a single orchestration notebook that runs all six silver transformation notebooks in sequence via dbutils.notebook.run, to serve as the silver layer entry point in Databricks Jobs.
requirements: List the 6 CRM/ERP silver notebook paths.
Iterate and call dbutils.notebook.run on each with timeout_seconds=0.
Use this notebook as the single job task for the silver layer.
preview: Chain all silver notebooks into one orchestrator with dbutils.notebook.run so the whole silver layer runs from a single Databricks Job task.
portfolio_value: Demonstrates notebook-based orchestration, the lightweight pattern teams use before adopting Jobs/DLT pipelines.
notes: Runs after bronze. dbutils.notebook.run requires the notebooks to be importable in the workspace at the given relative paths.

title: Gold Dimension: dim_customers (CRM+ERP join, surrogate key)
evaluates: Building a customer dimension in Spark SQL: joining CRM customers to ERP demographics and location, coalescing gender across sources, sourcing birthdate from ERP, and generating a ROW_NUMBER surrogate key.
requirements: LEFT JOIN silver.crm_customers to silver.erp_customers and silver.erp_customer_location on customer_number.
Prefer CRM gender, fall back to ERP gender, else n/a.
Generate customer_key via ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY customer_id).
Write workspace.gold.dim_customers as overwrite Delta.
preview: Model the customer dimension by joining CRM and ERP silver tables, coalescing gender, and minting a surrogate customer_key with ROW_NUMBER.
portfolio_value: Core dimensional-modeling skill: multi-source integration, attribute coalescing, and surrogate-key generation in Spark SQL.
notes: Reads three silver tables. customer_key is later referenced by fact_sales (via customer_id join in the fact).

title: Gold Dimension: dim_products (category enrichment, surrogate key)
evaluates: Building a product dimension in Spark SQL: enriching CRM products with ERP category/subcategory/maintenance via category_id, and generating a ROW_NUMBER surrogate key ordered by start_date and product_number.
requirements: LEFT JOIN silver.crm_products to silver.erp_product_category on category_id.
Select product attributes plus category, subcategory, maintenance_flag, product_line, start_date.
Generate product_key via ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY start_date, product_number).
Write workspace.gold.dim_products as overwrite Delta.
preview: Model the product dimension by enriching CRM products with ERP category data and assigning a surrogate product_key.
portfolio_value: Reinforces dimension building with reference enrichment and surrogate keys; includes a commented-out current-record filter as a discussion point.
notes: Reads two silver tables. A commented WHERE end_date IS NULL hints at SCD/current-version filtering not enabled here. product_key feeds fact_sales.

title: Gold Fact: fact_sales (join to dimensions on surrogate keys)
evaluates: Building the sales fact table in Spark SQL: joining silver sales to gold dim_products and dim_customers to attach surrogate keys, keeping order dates and measures (sales_amount, quantity, price).
requirements: LEFT JOIN silver.crm_sales to gold.dim_products on product_number and to gold.dim_customers on customer_id.
Project product_key, customer_key, order/ship/due dates and measures.
Write workspace.gold.fact_sales as overwrite Delta.
preview: Assemble the central fact table by joining silver sales to both gold dimensions on surrogate keys, completing the star schema.
portfolio_value: Demonstrates the keystone of dimensional modeling: linking facts to dimensions via surrogate keys to produce a query-ready star schema.
notes: Must run after both gold dimensions because it joins gold.dim_products and gold.dim_customers. Natural keys (product_number, customer_id) are used to look up the surrogate keys.

title: Gold Orchestration: Single Entry Point
evaluates: Building an orchestration notebook that runs the gold dimension and fact notebooks in the correct dependency order via dbutils.notebook.run.
requirements: List gold notebooks in order: dim_customers, dim_products, fact_sales.
Iterate and call dbutils.notebook.run on each with timeout_seconds=0.
Use this notebook as the single job task for the gold layer.
preview: Run the gold layer end to end with one orchestrator that executes the two dimensions before the fact, respecting the dependency order.
portfolio_value: Shows awareness of dependency ordering in orchestration (dimensions before facts), a common source of bugs for juniors.
notes: Runs after silver. Ordering matters: fact_sales depends on both gold dimensions existing first.
